=== baha ===
sha256 c3805471d17fbfa6286ce04b9c80d8bd373fdefcc68463e8cadb029b55ef86b8
baha - BaseHarbor command-line interface

Manage BaseHarbor and isolated application backend runtimes from one binary. Commands are
fail-closed: validation and preflight happen before mutation.

Usage:
  baha <command> [options]

Get started:
  new             Create an application, stack, target, provider, or workspace
  init            Initialize or adopt the application in the current repository
  list            List managed applications on the selected Target
  up              Converge selected application intent, or explicitly start the management Core

Understand and maintain:
  status          Show application status in a repository, otherwise control-plane status
  inspect         Inspect the current repository and its application requirements
  plan            Show the application plan in the current repository
  doctor          Diagnose the current application repository, otherwise the control plane
  update          Safely inspect or update BaseHarbor itself
  backup          Back up the current application through its managed lifecycle
  restore         Restore an application through the ownership-safe managed lifecycle
  destroy         Remove the complete BaseHarbor installation with explicit consequence consent
  down            Stop the current application, or the local control plane outside a repository

Advanced and operator commands:
  open            Open a verified HTTPS application endpoint
  logs            Show application logs for the current workload
  provider        Author and validate Capability Provider extensions
  stack           Discover and manage reusable development Stack Profiles
  workspace       Configure local workspace sources and repository mappings
  target          Inspect and manage BaseHarbor deployment targets
  env             Inspect and manage deployment-target environments
  use             Select and persist the active Core or deployment target
  node            Enroll and manage remote Docker or Podman nodes
  onboard         Guided onboarding: attach a workstation to a BaseHarbor installation
  workstation     Invite, list and revoke developer workstations connected to this Core
  user            Manage people and their enrolled workstations
  dev             Manage local development conveniences
  config          Configure BaseHarbor user preferences
  context         Select the per-terminal BaseHarbor context (Bash, Zsh or Fish)
  shell-init      Generate BaseHarbor shell integration for Bash, Zsh or Fish
  policy          Inspect the effective BaseHarbor policy for an application environment
  access          Guide profile assignment and deliberate offboarding of a person on a target
  agent           Discover the stable BaseHarbor machine interface
  mcp             Expose BaseHarbor semantic operations over MCP
  serve           Run the TLS-protected BaseHarbor runtime/control-plane API
  app             Manage declarative application backend runtimes
  connect         Allow one explicit application service to reach another
  disconnect      Remove one explicit cross-application connectivity exception
  connections     List explicit cross-application connectivity policy
  openbao         Bootstrap and operate the BaseHarbor OpenBao trust plane
  trust           Inspect, export or explicitly install the managed local BaseHarbor CA
  login           Authenticate the BaseHarbor operator through OIDC
  logout          Remove a local BaseHarbor operator session
  whoami          Show the authenticated BaseHarbor operator identity
  version         Print build version
  tui             Open the interactive BaseHarbor status dashboard
  completion      Generate shell completion for Bash, Zsh or Fish

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha access ===
sha256 79734c5dc0222e5d2a84caf7964771b34f587a1073eaf031f83188c99d5fea7b
access - Guide profile assignment and deliberate offboarding of a person on a target

Guided, fail-closed profile assignment and offboarding. The wizard names the person, searches and
selects declared Targets, confirms the effective rights, and reviews before any write. It never
grants a right on its own: every assignment folds into the single production policy authority and
every removal re-checks the current configuration at submit time.

Usage:
  baha access assign|--assign PERSON [--json] | baha access offboard|--offboard PERSON [--json]

Commands:
  assign    Guided assignment of an access profile to a person on selected Targets
  offboard  Guided deliberate offboarding of a person from a target

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha agent ===

agent - Discover the stable BaseHarbor machine interface

Exposes the versioned semantic operations that coding agents and automation may use safely.
Discovery describes BaseHarbor operations; it does not expose shell, Docker or Compose execution.

=== baha app ===
sha256 84b582c9cc1d88a9c811665cde9b718946d963e1dfdc2c9cf629b510e69e26ce
app - Manage declarative application backend runtimes

Applications are independent consumers of BaseHarbor. Put baseharbor.yaml in the application
repository and run app commands without NAME, or pass NAME explicitly for compatibility with stored
application state. Manifests contain desired backend services and required secret names, never
plaintext credentials.

Usage:
  baha app <command> [options]

Commands:
  new               Create a new ecosystem-native application from a BaseHarbor contract
  workspace         Manage local multi-repository workspace mappings
  init              Create the application contract or initialize deployment settings
  create            Create an application manifest in BaseHarbor state
  list              List registered deployments for the effective target
  show              Show a coherent application overview
  plan              Show desired resources without changing anything
  preflight         Validate an application before mutation
  edit              Edit current application needs with preview and impact consent
  footprint         Read the current application footprint
  inspect           Inspect a repository without changing it
  apply             Converge and verify an application's backend runtime
  backup            Create one encrypted recovery unit for an application
  restore           Restore and verify an encrypted application recovery unit
  env               Show the standard environment contract for an application
  sql               Open the managed SQL console for the current application
  cache             Open the managed cache console for the current application
  creds             Show connection metadata without revealing credentials by default
  secure-profile    Encrypt explicitly selected local credentials into a password-locked export
  export            Export selected local application credentials into an encrypted file
  logs              Show logs for the current application workload
  shell             Open a shell in an application workload service
  exec              Execute a command in an application workload service
  update            Safely inspect or update a Git-backed application
  pull              Safely pull Git source for the application, optionally bringing it up
  tls               Inspect and maintain application TLS certificates
  perses            Guide enable/status/disable and ownership-safe removal of the optional Perses
                    surface
  status            Show application runtime, readiness and version status
  doctor            Diagnose and safely repair an application's runtime
  down              Stop application runtimes while preserving data for reactivation
  stop              Stop application runtimes while preserving data for reactivation
  up                Start an existing application runtime and verify readiness
  destroy           Permanently remove an application and its exclusively owned data
  secret            Manage application secret values without printing them
  runtime-identity  Manage the app-scoped credential used for dynamic secret references
  evidence          Export secret-safe application lifecycle and verification evidence
  version           Show separated wanted/applied/observed release and component versions
  versions          Show readable wanted/applied/observed versions for recorded deployments
  prune             Remove a dangling deployment record whose source repository is gone
  urls              List verified application and service GUI URLs with their accessibility

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha app apply ===
sha256 e5c4d009530145451ce0e8705ab8640b2a63bf485e2873f1116ac74856b7f34a
apply - Converge and verify an application's backend runtime

Runs plan, preflight, apply and verification. Without NAME it resolves the nearest baseharbor.yaml
in the current repository, synchronizes a protected internal copy for runtime services, and treats
the repository manifest as the source of truth. When an unambiguous application Compose workload
exists, BaseHarbor generates a protected override, attaches it to the application backend network
when managed backend services exist and injects container-routable native service URLs.
Workload-only applications remain valid without inventing a managed database or cache. Declared
secrets.required entries are readiness gates. Explicit secrets.required[].generate entries are
created only when missing and are stored directly in OpenBao without printing their values.
Managed-secret workloads start only after the per-application mTLS broker has proven app-scoped
OpenBao readiness. For remote targets, --workload-port NAME=PORT selects and persists an explicit
free host port for this deployment. A repository-owned candidate submission is bound only on
explicit operator/automation confirmation: the apply prints the candidate's canonical content hash
and requires --confirm-candidate with that exact hash before writing any deployment state; without
the flag the apply fails closed.

Usage:
  baha app apply [NAME] [--skip-memory-preflight] [--confirm-candidate <digest>] [--workload-port NAME=PORT]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha app backup ===
sha256 07903374a862a852ee7f4fc9b8596c9cb2fe889a378f63af88facfefc9204b8d
backup - Create one encrypted recovery unit for an application

Creates one encrypted application recovery unit. In an interactive terminal, omitting
--password-file starts a guided flow with hidden password entry and safe output defaults. Automation
keeps using an owner-only --password-file; backup passwords are never accepted as command-line
values.

Usage:
  baha app backup [NAME] [--output FILE] [--password-file FILE] [--include-state CLASS] [--exclude-state CLASS]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output

  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:

=== baha app create ===
sha256 76914f9b04e073a9a93833f8c37e6f29fc18c8904d82e28d43d88edbd1b3484c
create - Create an application manifest in BaseHarbor state

Creates BaseHarbor-managed declarative application source on the effective Target; it does not start
containers. For a repository-owned source-of-truth manifest prefer 'baha app init'. Services are
requested explicitly; application identity is assigned by BaseHarbor.

Usage:
  baha app create NAME [--environment ENV] [--sql|--sql-instance NAME] [--cache|--cache-instance NAME] [--key-value|--key-value-instance NAME] [--document-db|--document-db-instance NAME] [--messaging-queue|--messaging-queue-instance NAME] [--messaging-pubsub|--messaging-pubsub-instance NAME] [--messaging-stream|--messaging-stream-instance NAME] [--s3|--s3-bucket NAME] [--secrets|--require-secret NAME]...

=== baha app destroy ===
sha256 3d6b75e0af23bc9c089716e8791c9cff69eed98098d3903525a4a5d978807da3
destroy - Permanently remove an application and its exclusively owned data

Permanently removes the application, its BaseHarbor-owned runtime resources, application data,
credentials, recovery state and deployment registration. Exclusively app-owned Compose data volumes
are removed too. Shared, foreign or ambiguously owned resources are preserved and reported. Use
'baha app stop' to stop runtime services while preserving data. Provider changes and permanent data
deletion require explicit approval of the current plan.

Usage:
  baha app destroy [NAME] [--uuid DEPLOYMENT-ID] [--yes]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha app doctor ===
sha256 90034c3dd8245275b1141e2c4d1acce861267371c6f78ba2973c49fbd26492ab
doctor - Diagnose and safely repair an application's runtime

Runs the existing application doctor, including required-secret presence/usability checks,
classifies failures using the same repair classes as root doctor, and with --fix only invokes the
normal guarded app apply lifecycle when every remaining failure is safely repairable. External
secrets, manifest or permission problems, and platform prerequisites remain fail-closed.

Usage:
  baha app doctor [NAME] [--fix --yes]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha app down ===
sha256 1c0ff69908f5badbacd5522199adbdd3835904ab15076a553d51d78633331a4d
down - Stop application runtimes while preserving data for reactivation

Stops the owned workload and provider runtime, releases its active provider references, and retains
persistent data, credentials, recovery material and the deployment owner so 'baha app apply' can
reactivate it. Pass --yes to execute; the current provider consequence plan still requires its own
acknowledgement. Use 'baha app destroy' to permanently delete app-owned data.

Usage:
  baha app down [NAME] [--yes]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha app env ===
sha256 c7356fe08e9ca409316d75e574fa4b313b8ca752deb1493e4caba23e43c2b61f
env - Show the standard environment contract for an application

Shows the native runtime contract generated by 'baha app apply'. Without NAME it resolves the
nearest repository baseharbor.yaml. Credential-bearing service URLs are masked by default; --reveal
prints the real values. --path prints only the absolute owner-only dotenv file path.

=== baha app evidence ===
sha256 fe233dfe18f6e9a1babdbcc55d0f9117ffe23b283b9f29268fc7a93fe9985eaa
evidence - Export secret-safe application lifecycle and verification evidence

Builds one deterministic, secret-safe evidence bundle from desired state, effective policy, observed
runtime state, verification results, recovery metadata and bounded lifecycle audit records. JSON
output is the generic export boundary; BaseHarbor does not provision a SIEM or vendor-specific
evidence sink.

Usage:
  baha app evidence [NAME] [-e ENV|--environment ENV] [-o json|--output json]

=== baha app exec ===
sha256 a17c2ca1cfa59e12c2109874e6c6689c5dca0db6578e8ea16d14082dd65f3c5d
exec - Execute a command in an application workload service

Runs COMMAND in the guided workload component; with no COMMAND the default interactive shell opens,
same as 'baha app shell'. Choose a component with COMPONENT or -c NAME. Put selector options before
COMMAND; once COMMAND starts, its remaining arguments, including flags such as Python's -c, are
passed through unchanged. A missing COMPONENT follows the same guidance and never blocks scripts.
--cmd takes exactly one command string and runs it through the workload's POSIX shell; it cannot be
combined with positional command arguments. The command's exit status is preserved: baha exits with
the same code the command returned.

Usage:
  baha app exec [--app NAME] [-e ENV|--environment ENV] [COMPONENT|-c NAME] [--cmd CMD|COMMAND [ARG...]]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha app export ===
sha256 d9847b22d0bd6d0b917f577f94c6758e648656575f7989a0ce910359ab13a264
export - Export selected local application credentials into an encrypted file

Opt-in, password-encrypted export of the eligible local credentials that exist for one application.
Selects only the local developer credentials that exist for the target/environment; never exports
remote provider secrets or fresh device identities by default, and never carries managed secret
values unless the caller passes the fail-closed human-authorization reveal seam. The export password
is read from a file (never argv); the ciphertext is unreadable without it. An export without any
selected source fails closed.

Usage:
  baha app export [NAME] [--include STATE]... --password-file FILE [--output FILE]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha app init ===
sha256 70bf4c9156eb5dfbd920de5b22790c5a5453daa20a2cf9bf09ca7e469dcecfda
init - Create the application contract or initialize deployment settings

Without an existing baseharbor.yaml, runs the normal guided application-contract generator. With an
existing repository manifest, asks only for the public FQDN and TLS settings. The --hostname flag is
kept for compatibility and accepts the public FQDN. Existing certificate mode accepts one directory;
BaseHarbor detects and validates the matching certificate/key pair and normalizes it under protected
local state. Deployment inputs are resolved through the reusable input resolver. --input supports
automation-safe injection for declared non-secret inputs such as hostname, tls_mode and cert_dir.
--agents creates or idempotently updates only the bounded BaseHarbor section in AGENTS.md. Without
baseharbor.yaml, the existing manifest flags remain available for deterministic repository-contract
creation.

Usage:
  baha app init --agents [--json] | baha app init [--quick] [--json] | baha app init [--input NAME=VALUE]... [--hostname HOST] [--tls acme|existing|local] [--cert-dir DIR] [--yes] | baha app init [NAME] [-e ENV|--environment ENV] [--sql|--sql-instance NAME] [--cache|--cache-instance NAME] [--key-value|--key-value-instance NAME] [--document-db|--document-db-instance NAME] [--messaging-queue|--messaging-queue-instance NAME] [--messaging-pubsub|--messaging-pubsub-instance NAME] [--messaging-stream|--messaging-stream-instance NAME] [--s3|--s3-bucket NAME] [--secrets|--require-secret NAME] [--workload-component NAME]... [--workload-source KIND:PATH]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead

=== baha app logs ===
sha256 d2533c36076445924deb0c6d06dfbe9dd79f54b77d1b466f71cf7fb0f75eda6d
logs - Show logs for the current application workload

Reads application logs through the same read-view logic 'baha app status' renders: the deployment
log policy decides the source and the application contract decides the streamable components. A
missing COMPONENT is guided - a unique declared component is derived, ambiguity lists the options in
a terminal, and --no-input or scripts never block and fail closed with the options. --tail N bounds
the output to the N most recent lines and finishes. -c filters the stream to the named components.
JSON output never follows: unbounded streaming has no JSON contract; bounded --tail reads do.
Managed (Loki) collection is reported explicitly, never silently rerouted.

Usage:
  baha app logs [COMPONENT] [--follow] [--tail N] [-c NAME]... [--app NAME] [-e ENV|--environment ENV] [--json]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha app perses ===
sha256 31499850fcaf6915bb4763c2492921deff0dbf04b67d0f3041635f40ceb1c379
perses - Guide enable/status/disable and ownership-safe removal of the optional Perses surface

Guided lifecycle for the optional Perses observability management surface. Enable selects the
optional Perses realization of the observability management-ui surface; disable deselects it (the
surface returns to not_configured); status reports the public three-state contract; remove disables
the surface and retires only the BaseHarbor-owned Perses runtime resources, preserving Prometheus,
Loki, Tempo and foreign data. Fail-closed: an unauthorized or unresolved-ownership caller fails
before any manifest mutation. Perses remains optional and never forces a new application capability.

Usage:
  baha app perses <command> [NAME] [--json]

Commands:
  enable   Select the optional Perses management-ui surface
  disable  Deselect the optional Perses management-ui surface
  status   Report Perses state and live alert-rule health
  remove   Ownership-safe retirement of the owned Perses surface

=== baha app prune ===
sha256 90d1238e07389f16629f88f63b0ad933c7f6d09ec4308c07943723fed22a2b43
prune - Remove a dangling deployment record whose source repository is gone

Removes a SINGLE dangling deployment record whose source repository is no longer available. The
record can no longer be resolved by the source-required lifecycle commands
(apply/update/plan/preflight/init) and cannot be destroyed or downed, so it stays permanently
uncollectable and `baha app list` keeps showing MISSING. prune removes ONLY that registry record: it
never touches runtime, containers, volumes, identities, secrets, provider bindings or any other
deployment record. It refuses when the source repository is still present (the deployment is
recoverable) and when the given name matches more than one record (naming each). Exactly one name is
required.

Usage:
  baha app prune <name>

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha app pull ===
sha256 3e213edcfa8c10005a7f00c4f797f9ce0741aea48d426dde9929628877657143
pull - Safely pull Git source for the application, optionally bringing it up

Selects repository or local sources by component and pulls each selected source as a strict
fast-forward to its upstream, inspecting working-tree, branch, upstream and divergence first. The
working tree must be clean; a dirty, ahead or diverged source blocks that source without touching
others. --check previews the pull plan without changing source. With --up the application is brought
up using the same app-up operation as 'baha app update', only after every selected source pulled
successfully. Non-interactive: a blocker is an actionable error, never a prompt. No secret values
are printed.

Usage:
  baha app pull [-c COMPONENT[,COMPONENT...]] [--up] [--check] [--manifest PATH] [-o json|--output json]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha app up ===
sha256 08f372972e75507f3f0306c1200fb2db6db5c0584e98c57707d4078457f93052
up - Start an existing application runtime and verify readiness

Starts a previously materialized BaseHarbor application runtime using its existing runtime
definition, credentials and persistent data; required application secrets are verified before
workload start and missing values fail closed. Repository workloads are started after their
BaseHarbor backend and per-application secret broker are ready. Workload-only applications skip the
empty managed-runtime start and resume their repository Compose workload directly. Without NAME it
resolves the nearest repository baseharbor.yaml. --yes accepts allowed confirmations but never
invents unresolved selections or operator authentication configuration.

Usage:

=== baha app update ===
sha256 e8ce8c86a4b25d0f4eef44890431e220414f51bd92fbfa63a39528d45a7eef47
update - Safely inspect or update a Git-backed application

Fetches only the configured upstream remote and verifies repository, branch, revision and
working-tree state before any mutation. --check reports the update plan without changing source. For
applications with durable managed PostgreSQL or secrets, mutation requires either an encrypted
pre-update recovery point through --backup-password-file FILE or an explicit --no-backup
acknowledgement. The source update is strict fast-forward-only to the exact fetched target revision,
followed by the normal application apply/readiness lifecycle. BaseHarbor never resets, stashes,
discards local changes, switches branches, merges divergent history or rebases implicitly.

Usage:
  baha app update [--check] [--backup-password-file FILE | --no-backup]

sha256 29232d6e3f7b69490f1e01fd7c3289e4c123d696e75d2c6d06c273353f53138d
urls - List verified application and service GUI URLs with their accessibility

Lists the application's own URLs and the GUI URLs of its bound app/shared services from the same
secret-safe read view 'baha app status' renders. Every entry carries verified or unverified
accessibility; nothing is guessed, invented or opened. --print emits only the verified URLs

version - Show separated wanted/applied/observed release and component versions

Read-only version view of one deployment. Wanted, applied and observed come from the three
independent recorded reference dimensions and are never copied between each other. A dimension
without a recorded version shows an explicit UNCLEAR cell instead of a blank. Component rows carry
their portable source-model provenance (source id, kind, identity) or an explicit unmapped state;
observed runtime identity enriches the same rows when reachable. An unknown -c component fails
closed. Metadata claims are labeled unverified; no Git revision is inferred from a tag.

=== baha app workspace ===
sha256 856279047eff9b8bee3c5cdb0351698d0ae03e41657404f781df706c8dd661c4
workspace - Manage local multi-repository workspace mappings

With no subcommand, opens the guided multi-repository workspace setup. Portable source identity is
kept in .baseharbor/sources.yaml while developer-local checkout paths stay in XDG configuration and
never become Application Intent. Sources are Git repositories, local directories or OCI images;
components are optional unique identities and several components may share one source.

  baha app workspace [<init|map|show|resolve|status|update|path|source|component> [options]]

Commands:
  init       Create versioned source identity metadata for a multi-repository application
  map        Map one repository source identity to an existing local checkout/worktree
  show       Show canonical source identities and local workspace mappings
  resolve    Resolve component source identity to local worktrees without using the current working
             directory
  status     Inspect Git state for all mapped repository sources
  update     Safely fast-forward mapped Git repositories
  path       Set or show the local path of one source (checkout mapping or directory source)
  source     Add or remove individual application sources

  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output

  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details

  --no-color          Disable ANSI color

=== baha context ===
sha256 df5c313f39403cc881ff627cabfe98d3bbbd9aa65b6d47bdcb431a9cec1d4e69
context - Select the per-terminal BaseHarbor context (Bash, Zsh or Fish)

Select the per-terminal deployment context without changing the per-user persisted selection.
'context use' prints the shell snippet that sets BASEHARBOR_TARGET for the current shell process
only; with the one-time hook installed via 'baha completion bash|zsh|fish' the shell evaluates that
snippet automatically, so each independent terminal keeps its own selection in its own environment.
'context clear' unsets the selection in the current process and prints a hint. 'context show'
reports the effective selection and which precedence level won.

Usage:
  baha context use [--shell bash|zsh|fish] TARGET | clear | show

Commands:
  use    Emit the per-terminal activation snippet for TARGET
  clear  Clear the per-terminal selection in the current process
  show   Report the effective per-terminal selection and winning precedence level

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output

  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output

destroy - Remove the complete BaseHarbor installation with explicit consequence consent

Removes registered applications, owned providers and runtime resources, Core services, and

=== baha login ===
sha256 3ccfabf731601ce84a8ee9cbc4278280cb106cde61ce0f41abd7bc15083abcbf
login - Authenticate the BaseHarbor operator through OIDC

Authenticates through Authorization Code + PKCE. --init-tenant is an explicit first-owner operation,
restricted to the locally owned management Core after real OIDC login; it creates exactly one
initial tenant and editor membership. --ca trusts the managed CA the Core bootstrapped without OS
system-trust surgery (BASEHARBOR_OPERATOR_OIDC_CA_FILE is the state-wide alias). On non-browser
hosts complete the PKCE flow headless with --auth-code-file (or
BASEHARBOR_OPERATOR_OIDC_AUTH_CODE_FILE) and --no-browser; a fixed loopback callback port is honored
via BASEHARBOR_OPERATOR_OIDC_CALLBACK_PORT. Existing trusted local dev without an operator OIDC
configuration remains login-free.

Usage:
  baha login -e ENV|--environment ENV [--init-tenant] [--tenant-slug SLUG] [--tenant-name NAME] [--ca FILE] [--auth-code-file FILE] [--no-browser]

=== baha onboard ===
sha256 ddcd3ce7a71b19fbb656f0548ebb6da1f719d17d0f99269b2ee91458a6190441
onboard - Guided onboarding: attach a workstation to a BaseHarbor installation

On the Core host, --invite creates a new Keycloak user and first workstation. It asks for the
person's full name, login, email, device name and certificate lifetime, then securely prompts for an
initial password. The password is temporary and must be changed at first login. Email is contact
information only; SMTP is not required. Use baha workstation new to add another device for an
existing person. On a developer workstation, --import redeems the private one-use device invitation.

Usage:
  baha onboard [--target NAME] [--json] | baha onboard --import PRIVATE_FILE [--target-name NAME] [--trust-host-ca|--skip-host-trust] [--configure-hosts|--skip-hosts] | baha onboard --invite [--name PERSON] [--login LOGIN] [--email EMAIL] [--station DEVICE] [--certificate-ttl 5y] [--output PRIVATE_FILE] | baha onboard --init-tenant [-e ENV] [--tenant-slug SLUG --tenant-name NAME]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output

=== baha openbao bootstrap ===
sha256 e51c5847ac5df1e03ee00acdad8a457ce5e7245098c806d1454c16b3640dd52e
bootstrap - Initialize OpenBao and establish the BaseHarbor manager identity

Initializes the bundled single-node OpenBao instance with one Shamir key share, stores only the
unseal material in the explicitly selected owner-only recovery file, configures the baseharbor KV v2
mount and a restricted manager AppRole, verifies that identity, and revokes the initial root token.
The recovery file must be outside .baseharbor state. Options: --recovery-file PATH Required
destination for OpenBao unseal recovery material

Usage:
  baha openbao bootstrap --recovery-file PATH

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

sha256 639a295913c3396b66a11b6fd3101961645c31776aed7d1270d67a685dc79908
rotate - Rotate OpenBao/control-plane credentials and managed service PKI

Rotates the restricted OpenBao manager AppRole credential, PostgreSQL control-plane
administration/replication/OpenBao-storage credentials, and the managed service CA. Replacement
credentials and trust are verified before previous material is retired. Secret values are never
printed. Options: --recovery-file PATH Required owner-only OpenBao recovery file used if a rolling
member restart requires unseal

Usage:
  baha openbao rotate --recovery-file PATH

serve - Run the TLS-protected BaseHarbor runtime/control-plane API

Starts the TLS-protected BaseHarbor application runtime API. A managed per-application broker is
bound to one app/environment, requires mTLS plus the app runtime token, and authenticates to OpenBao
only with that application's AppRole. Configure OIDC audiences plus a database URL only for the
separate operator control-plane API. For the operator API on a Core host, see the runbook:
https://mcpdev80.github.io/baseharbor/how-to/operator-api/.

sha256 501cfe3771b9c7b0fac14b51cc0fc596d25a01947adf83260097319d9df7af35
trust - Inspect, export or explicitly install the managed local BaseHarbor CA

Operates only on public trust material for the managed-local issuer. Private CA keys remain inside
the issuer provider. External PKI and BYOC trust roots are never claimed or installed as
BaseHarbor-owned host trust.

Usage:
  baha trust <status|export|install|uninstall> [options]

Commands:
  status     Show whether the managed-local CA is trusted by this host
  export     Export only the public managed-local CA certificate
  install    Explicitly install the public CA into system and supported browser trust stores
  uninstall  Remove only BaseHarbor-owned host trust anchors

=== baha up ===
sha256 348857ee185d33f95074f4c8684c87b9c123a006f259bc56d1c7255e1b7527c6
up - Converge selected application intent, or explicitly start the management Core

Inside an application repository, converges selected capabilities and genuine dependencies through
the same current-plan acknowledgement, authorization and verification as app apply. It does not
install a management Core merely because an application exists. Unresolved deployment inputs use the
existing guided resolver; --yes does not replace provider-consequence or data-deletion consent. In a
detected project without baseharbor.yaml, interactive use initializes the application through the
existing guided flow; --yes uses unambiguous safe defaults. Directories without application signals
retain explicit management setup. --control-plane-only explicitly selects the independent
SQL/Secrets/Identity management installation and its HA, port, recovery and host-trust options.
--trust-host-ca remains a separate explicit opt-in; --yes never changes host trust. -e/--environment
selects resolved deployment state without rewriting authored intent.

Usage:
  baha up [NAME] [-e ENV|--environment ENV] [--yes] [--skip-memory-preflight] [--control-plane-only] [--ha] [--trust-host-ca] [--postgres-port PORT] [--openbao-port PORT] [--recovery-file PATH]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output

=== baha update ===
sha256 81c16fea2690a985ad1913b6d1ec9a5423cc56a124f74b6819e9fec98bc54862
update - Safely inspect or update BaseHarbor itself

Checks or installs published BaseHarbor releases. Stable is the default channel; prereleases are
considered only when --channel rc or an explicit prerelease --version is supplied. Mutation requires
--yes, verifies release checksums and the candidate binary before replacement, retains a recovery
binary, and verifies the updated CLI/runtime before reporting success. --recover --version VERSION
--yes explicitly restores the owned Core HA PostgreSQL and DCS to that update's verified backup
point, retains displaced volumes, and does not replace the CLI. Transactions after that backup point
are not included.

Usage:
  baha update [--check] [--yes] [--channel stable|rc | --version VERSION] [--recover]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha workspace ===
sha256 5310f5a1e4d65e77555679918cbf0abcc5aa7647da4c9737c7db3b9300e46e01
workspace - Configure local workspace sources and repository mappings

With no subcommand, opens the guided multi-repository workspace setup. Portable source identity is
kept in .baseharbor/sources.yaml while developer-local checkout paths stay in XDG configuration and
never become Application Intent. Sources are Git repositories, local directories or OCI images;
components are optional unique identities and several components may share one source.

Usage:
  baha workspace [<init|map|show|resolve|status|update|path|source|component> [options]]

Commands:
  init       Create versioned source identity metadata for a multi-repository application
  map        Map one repository source identity to an existing local checkout/worktree
  show       Show canonical source identities and local workspace mappings
  resolve    Resolve component source identity to local worktrees without using the current working
             directory
  status     Inspect Git state for all mapped repository sources
  update     Safely fast-forward mapped Git repositories
  path       Set or show the local path of one source (checkout mapping or directory source)
  source     Add or remove individual application sources
  component  Inspect and maintain unique component-to-source mappings

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.

=== baha workspace update ===
sha256 88c3061c92e76916b6b7343488df8b1f729b2c7ba3a845f0f2ad9236d0cfbe7b
update - Safely fast-forward mapped Git repositories

Fetches each mapped repository using native Git. Clean branches with a configured upstream are
updated only when a strict fast-forward is possible. BaseHarbor never stashes, resets, switches
branches, rebases, merges divergent history or resolves conflicts.

Usage:
  baha workspace update [--manifest PATH] [--check] [-o json|--output json]

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

=== baha workstation ===
sha256 fdc9e04ac8b451cf71c31cec658698d8ee93dee86a16f9ecc7715c232b76a585
workstation - Invite, list and revoke developer workstations connected to this Core

Run on the Core host. New adds a device for an existing user. List shows each enrolled workstation,
its owner and certificate expiry. Revoke disables that workstation's current certificate and
immediately verifies the result.

Usage:
  baha workstation new | baha workstation list | baha workstation revoke NAME [--yes]

Commands:
  new     Issue a one-use invitation for another workstation owned by an existing user
  list    List enrolled workstations and certificate expiry
  revoke  Revoke a workstation's current certificate

Global options:
  -q, --quiet         Suppress progress and non-essential human output
  --silent            Alias for --quiet
  -v, --verbose       Show diagnostic runtime details
  --plain             Stable styling-free line-oriented human output
  --no-color          Disable ANSI color
  --no-input          Never prompt; fail with an actionable error instead
  --version           Print the BaseHarbor version

Help:
  Use '<command> --help' for command-specific help.
